title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using the declared model "gpt-5-mini" and a deterministic rule-based validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks, the validator flagged 719/720 (0.9986111111111111) and the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation, with a single allowed repair-stage call) flagged 720/720 (1.0). The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair). These artifact-grounded outcomes lie well below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, clarified audit accounting for shared-generation semantics, an artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and prescriptive boundary conditions for when sandboxed emulation is most likely to add value. The canonical execution bundle and analysis artifacts are archived with the run for independent verification.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to convert operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment of such pipelines demands assurance that generated artifacts are syntactically correct, preserve required ordering/workflows, and satisfy higher‑order safety and policy invariants. A widely advocated mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, occasionally augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports document this pattern and motivate workflow‑centred evaluation [1]–[3], but there is limited large‑scale, preregistered evidence quantifying the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed execution to an already strong deterministic validator. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment that isolates downstream guarded-stage effects by enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics: every paired comparison reuses the identical initial sampled candidate so any between-condition discordance can only arise after generation (emulation observations or permitted repair). Our contributions are: (1) a machine‑readable preregistration and autonomous execution; (2) an artifact‑grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720; (3) clarified run-accounting and provider‑call audit interpretation under shared generation; and (4) an evidence‑based discussion of boundary conditions where guarded stages are or are not beneficial.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys, architectural reports, and prototype systems document the adoption of validator- and emulator‑assisted workflows for LLM‑generated NetOps artifacts. Work on combining generation with verification and repair spans program/specification domains and emerging NetOps prototypes; authors emphasize that correctness is multidimensional—syntax, command ordering/workflow constraints, invariants, and dynamic runtime properties each require distinct V&V primitives [1]–[3]. Prototype case studies report heterogeneous gains from emulation: in some task regimes static validators already catch most hazards, while in others emulation uncovers subtle runtime failures not expressible as static rules. These observations motivated our paired design that isolates only the downstream contribution of sandboxed emulation under a fixed initial candidate.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and paired design. We preregistered a paired binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistration fixed sample size (Npairs = 720), inclusion/exclusion rules (parser acceptance with up to two deterministic reseeds), missingness handling, multiplicity treatment for exploratory secondary tests, contamination controls, and a minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 used for power planning. The design enforces shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair we obtain exactly one sampled initial candidate and present that same candidate to (A) the baseline validator-only pipeline and (B) the guarded pipeline (validator followed by sandboxed emulation and, where permitted, one repair-stage model call). This isolates guarded-stage effects by removing generation variability as a source of between-condition discordance.

Task bank, topology and vendor abstractions. Confirmatory items were produced deterministically by a task generator from an intent_configuration_repair family; the bank spans three abstracted vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3‑node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit intent, a required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make‑before‑break). Inclusion required vendor parser acceptance after deterministic reseeding; the confirmatory run had zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and yielded complete_pair_count = 720.

Validator, emulator, and repair policy. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) applies deterministic rule checks: vendor CLI parsing, canonical per‑command parsing, sequence‑order checks against required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints (make‑before‑break, all_down_before_any_field_change), protected‑interface invariants, group‑activity constraints, and final‑state conformance. The guarded pipeline runs the same validator and then, irrespective of validator output, executes the candidate in a sandboxed emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology template and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor‑abstracted virtual devices. The emulator reports runtime observations (interface state transitions, transient downtime, MTU/VLAN application effects, and basic reachability consequences) and maps a conservative set of observation patterns to guarded detections. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task; repair calls are recorded in run accounting.

Provider-call auditing and shared-initial accounting (clarification). The run records provider model call events in a provider_call_audit object that counts events by stage (stage_counts) and by event-type labels used by the orchestration adapter (condition_counts). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the initial sampled generation is a single provider call shared by both downstream conditions and is therefore recorded under the stage label for shared initial generation; any subsequent model calls (repairs or guarded-only regenerations, if allowed) are recorded under their respective stage labels. In our execution the provider-call audit reports 721 total model-call events: 720 for shared initial generation and 1 repair-stage call. The condition_counts field records provider-call events by orchestration label (e.g., events initiated during the shared_initial stage versus events initiated during guarded stages) and is not a per-condition episode success count. This explains the apparent asymmetry where shared initial events are large while guarded-stage events are small: the shared initial call was used once per pair and presented identically to both baseline and guarded pipelines, while the single additional model call corresponds to the single permitted repair invocation across the entire confirmatory set. Complete_pair_count = 720 continues to enumerate paired episodes; provider_call_audit summarizes model-call events and is reconciled with paired accounting via deterministic_reconciliation checks archived with the execution artifacts.

Analysis procedures. The primary analysis used a paired-binary executor aligned with McNemar-style inference and cluster-robust variance estimation. We computed the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline), applied a two-sided exact McNemar test, and produced a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Pre-registered sensitivity analyses exist for missingness handling; no irrecoverable technical pairs occurred in the confirmatory run.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and exact statistics (artifact-derived). The paired contingency counts are: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting reports model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These numeric outputs are the direct archived analysis results from the preregistered analysis executor.

Discordant-pair attribution and repair accounting. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, any discordant pair must arise from downstream guarded-stage activity: a guarded-only emulation observation or the single permitted repair-stage invocation. Provider-call accounting shows the single additional model call (the lone repair invocation) coincides with the unique n10 discordant count. The canonical execution bundle contains per-episode traces that allow an auditor to locate that specific pair_id and inspect validator_trace and any repair transcript to determine whether the guarded detection followed an emulation observation or a repair-induced change. For succinctness in this manuscript we refer auditors to the archived execution manifest and canonical execution bundle to inspect that mapping; no raw log excerpts or file hashes are reproduced here.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded interpretation for a near-zero guarded benefit. The negligible aggregate guarded-stage benefit observed (≈0.0014) appears to arise from three artifact-evident factors: (1) validator ceiling effect: the deterministic validator explicitly encoded the workflow constraints exercised by the curated tasks, producing a baseline success rate of 719/720 that leaves almost no headroom for guarded-stage detection gains; (2) curated inclusion and low adversarial exposure: confirmatory items were parser-validated deterministic tasks, reducing the prevalence of runtime-only faults that emulation would reveal in noisier or adversarial distributions; (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics and minimal repair activity: the paired design isolates only downstream differences, and only a single repair-stage call occurred across the run. Operational implication: when a high‑coverage static validator is aligned to a constrained, parser‑validated task distribution, automated sandboxed emulation may add little marginal detection value at scale. However, this conclusion is narrowly scoped: in regimes with noisy natural-language intents, adversarial inputs, broader vendor/CLI diversity, or long‑lived stateful interactions, guarded emulation is more likely to surface faults not captured by static rules.

Recommendations grounded in the artifacts. For low-latency, high-throughput intent→configuration pipelines where inputs are tightly prevalidated, investment in richer static validators can be an efficient mitigation. For high‑impact or high‑risk changes, selective guarded sandboxing remains prudent. We suggest targeted follow-ups that the archived run can seed: adversarial/fuzzing task banks to enumerate validator gaps, broader vendor‑CLI coverage to challenge parser/validator assumptions, and higher‑fidelity emulation models of vendor control-plane behaviors.

Threats to validity tied to the execution choices. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate guarded-stage effects but omit any benefits from independent guarded-stage re‑generation. Construct validity: our binary detection metric depends on the validator and emulation rule-mappings and may underrepresent less tangible runtime harms. External validity: single declared/requested model family and single validator implementation limit generalizability. Conclusion validity: the study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed effect lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near‑zero result for this experimental regime rather than a general negative finding against sandboxing.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 720) that enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and used a strong deterministic validator, augmenting the validator with an automated sandboxed-emulation stage yielded a vanishing marginal detection gain (paired difference ≈ 0.0014; exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.00417]). Run accounting shows only one repair-stage model call across the confirmatory set. These artifact-grounded outcomes indicate that, under the studied constrained and parser-validated regime, a validator ceiling effect explains the negligible guarded benefit. Whether guarded emulation provides meaningful incremental coverage in adversarial or production-like regimes remains an open empirical question and is recommended as follow-up work using adversarial task banks and expanded vendor/emulation fidelity. The archived execution and analysis artifacts provide auditable inputs for such follow‑ups and for independent verification of the results.

Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded by the run). Deterministic validator used: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration identifier: f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e. Immutable initial master-prompt reference archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The autonomous pipeline carried out literature review, preregistration, code and prompt synthesis, execution, analysis, autonomous peer review, and manuscript drafting after the autonomy lock; a human Research Director selected the high-level NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock prompt. All per-episode outputs, run accounting, and analysis artifacts are archived in the canonical execution bundle referenced by the run’s execution manifest; that bundle contains the raw generated artifacts, validator and emulator traces, provider-call audit, and the analysis artifacts that support every numeric claim in this paper. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator‑ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and a single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrow finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.
Residual provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain possible despite audit controls; these residual uncertainties are documented in the archived reconciliation artifacts.
